issues.description: The problem statement specifies calculateTotalPrice(Meal) should return a double (mentions "double precision" and the UML shows : double), but the reference solution implements calculateTotalPrice as returning an int. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected return type and may cause grading/tests to expect a double while the solution uses int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature and implementation consistent with the specification: change calculateTotalPrice to return double (public static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)), use a double accumulator (e.g., double sum = 0.0) and return a double. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to specify an int return type if integer prices are intended. Prefer changing the implementation to double to match the stated requirement of double precision.
